references.text: The Lord your God will drive out these nations before you little by little. You cannot destroy them all at once, or the wild animals would become too numerous for you.
Previous verse explaining why the expulsion happens gradually - so that the land does not become desolate and wild animals multiply.
The promise that Abraham's offspring will become numerous and inherit the land, fulfilled through the gradual expansion described here.
Israel's fertility and multiplication in Egypt, which is a prerequisite for them to fill and inherit the land.
The promise that the Lord will drive out nations and that Israel will inherit the land where they set their foot.
Fulfillment of the promise where Joshua reminds the people that they received a land they did not work for.
Command to drive out the inhabitants of the land and take possession of it as an inheritance.
Exodus 23:30 shows the practical unfolding of the covenantal promise of numerousness from Genesis 17:6 as a prerequisite for taking possession of the land.
Ezekiel 36:24 serves as a new fulfillment of the principle in Exodus 23:30, where God again takes the initiative to bring the people back to the land after they have lost it.
Numbers 33:53 confirms the goal (to take possession of the land) for which Exodus 23:30 describes the process to achieve.
Deuteronomy 28:63 uses language from Exodus 23:30 (numerousness and taking possession of the land) to create a powerful contrast between God's blessing and his judgment.
Deuteronomy 4:38 confirms the action (to drive out peoples) that Exodus 23:30 describes with specific tactics and reasoning.
Joshua 23:5 is a direct summary and confirmation of the principle in Exodus 23:30 that God himself drives out enemies to give Israel the land.
